activities.anchor: A word's meaning has at least two distinct parts
activities.caption: pair each expression with what it shows
activities.name: semSenseMatch

config.prompt: Frege's split at work — pair the expression with what it demonstrates:

pairs.right: what the word points at in the world
the mode of presentation — the description under which Venus is picked out

pairs.left: 'the morning star IS the evening star'
pairs.right: an informative identity: same referent, different senses
sense without a referent — meaning with nothing pointed at

config.why: Meaning is not just the thing pointed at — which is why identity claims can inform and empty names can still mean.

activities.anchor: Within the lexicon, meanings relate in patterned ways
activities.caption: file each relation by the pattern it runs on
activities.name: semLexBuckets

config.prompt: Testable relations in the lexicon — file each:

items.label: a spaniel is a hyponym of dog, which is a hyponym of animal
a 'bachelor' pope or a stranded male seal strains the analysis
the relation dictionaries and ontologies are built from

config.why: Word meaning is partly world knowledge, not just features — that is where the classic puzzle leaks.

activities.anchor: From truth conditions flow the entailment relations
activities.caption: true or false — the logical baseline
activities.name: semEntailJudge

statements.why: True in every situation the first is true — entailment needs no speaker.
The two cannot be true in the same world.
It is compatible with either — a third relation, weaker than contradiction.

statements.s: 'Cats kill mice' means different things in different contexts.
statements.why: Its truth conditions stay fixed across contexts — that fixity is what pragmatics operates against.

activities.anchor: That principle is why you can understand sentences you have never heard
activities.caption: drag the divider — one sentence, two scopes
activities.name: semScopeCompare

config.prompt: Compositionality's edge case — drag the divider between the readings:

before.label: Reading 1 — for each man, some possibly-different woman
before.text: 'Every' takes scope over 'a' — the default reading.

after.label: Reading 2 — one particular woman for all men
after.text: 'A' takes wide scope — same words, two scope assignments.

config.why: Exactly parallel to the structural ambiguity the syntax lesson found in trees, but computed over meanings.

activities.anchor: The power of the scheme is what happens when a maxim is
activities.caption: find the line Grice would correct
activities.name: semMaximSpot

config.prompt: One line of this maxims summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Quantity: be informative — say as much as the exchange requires.
A maxim violation must stay hidden for the message to land.
config.correction: Flouting is open violation the hearer cannot miss — assume cooperation and the violation itself becomes the message.
config.why: Irony and metaphor flout quality ('Lovely weather' in a downpour): meaning is recovered by assuming truthfulness at a higher level.

activities.caption: order the scale the inference rides on
activities.name: semScaleOrder

config.prompt: Ordered scales under the inference — arrange weakest to strongest:
config.why: Saying the weaker term implicates the stronger was not available — the same logic orders possibly–probably–certainly and warm–hot. The diagnostic is cancellability: the vanishing-without-contradiction inference that law, contracts and journalism all lean on.

activities.caption: true or false — what travels beneath
activities.name: semPresupJudge

statements.s: 'John's brother is tall' presupposes that John has a brother.
statements.why: Content beneath the main assertion — it travels whether or not the assertion is agreed with.

statements.s: 'John's brother isn't tall' no longer presupposes the brother exists.
statements.why: Presupposition survives negation — projection is the test.

statements.s: Presuppositions project through questions and negation; implicatures cancel.
statements.why: The field's cleanest separation of meaning layers.

statements.s: The loaded question is a modern rhetorical invention.
statements.why: The rhetorical uses are ancient — the frame that contains the assumption before the debate begins.

activities.caption: resolve the pronoun — walk the inference
activities.name: semAnaphoraBranch

config.root: One pronoun, two candidates — walk the resolution.

start.text: 'Mary told Susan that her car was ready.' Which owner does 'her' prefer?

choices.label: Mary — the subject
choices.feedback: Preference runs the other way: 'her' leans to the nearer antecedent.

choices.label: Susan — the nearer name
choices.feedback: Right as a default — but preference is not grammar.

pref.text: 'Mary told Susan that she herself was ready' flips it; 'Mary said to Susan that her flight left at six' could genuinely be either — real conversation resolves it with stress, context or repair ('her — my — flight'). This is anaphora: referring back with reduced material.

bridge.text: 'We stopped for lunch. The waiter was rude.' Nothing introduced a waiter — bridging manufactures one from the inference: restaurants have waiters. Every sentence of connected discourse leans on these inferences.

config.why: The context does the work the words omit — and machines that resolve 'it' correctly are doing pragmatics, while the ones that fail are doing dictionary lookup.
